title: National Treasure
tagline: One old map. One long lunch.
about: A treasure hunter finds a map on the back of the Declaration of Independence and has to steal it first.
cue: Serve the snacks when Ben brushes lemon juice on the back of the Declaration.

    StartersInvisible ink lemon chicken bitesGrilled lemon oregano chicken pieces on toothpicks, lemon mayo to dipHow to make it600g chicken thighs, cut into chunks2 lemons, one for the marinade and one for the sauce3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tbsp dried oregano3 tbsp olive oil150g mayonnaiseMarinate the chicken in lemon juice, garlic, oregano and oil for an hour.Grill until charred and cooked through.Mix the mayonnaise with lemon zest and juice. Spear the chicken on toothpicks and serve with the sauce.Silence Dogood soft pretzelsSoft figure-eight pretzels with rock salt, butter and yellow mustardHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast300ml warm water1 tsp salt2 tbsp bicarb soda1 tbsp rock salt40g butter, melted4 tbsp yellow mustardMix the flour, yeast, salt and warm water to a dough and knead briefly. Rest for an hour.Shape into figure eights.Dip in boiling water with the bicarb soda and sprinkle with rock salt.Bake at 220°C for 12 minutes. Brush with butter and serve with mustard.Arctic ship clam chowder cupsThe old ship buried in the Arctic iceHow to make itAs written, serves 4Creamy chowder of bacon, potato, onion and clams finished with cream and thyme, served in small cups with oyster crackers on top.Steam 1kg clams in 250ml water in a covered pot for 5 minutes until open, then pick out the meat and strain the liquid.Fry 150g diced bacon, add 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks and soften.Add 500g diced potatoes, the clam liquid and 500ml milk, and simmer 15 minutes.Stir in 150ml cream, the clams and thyme, and season.Serve in cups with oyster crackers.Mains2:22 Independence Hall cheesesteaksShaved rib eye with onion and melted provolone on long rollsHow to make it600g rib eye steak2 brown onions, sliced2 tbsp oil150g provolone, sliced4 long bread rollsFreeze the steak for 30 minutes, then shave it paper thin.Fry the onions in the oil until soft.Add the beef and sear fast on high heat.Lay the provolone over the top to melt and pile into split rolls.Founding Fathers chicken and leek pot pieThe Founding Fathers' hidden cluesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken, leek and mushroom in a creamy thyme sauce, baked under a golden puff pastry lid, with buttered peas on the side.Brown 800g diced chicken thighs, then remove.Soften 2 sliced leeks and 200g mushrooms in 40g butter, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml chicken stock and 150ml cream.Simmer until thick, add thyme and the chicken, and season.Pour into a pie dish, top with a puff pastry sheet, brush with egg and cut a slit.Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes.Serve with 400g buttered peas.SweetsPhilly lemon water iceFrozen lemon ice scraped fluffy with a fork as it freezesHow to make it250g caster sugar750ml water250ml lemon juice2 lemons, zested, from the 8 lemons in total125g raspberriesBoil the water and sugar until dissolved, then cool. Stir in the lemon juice and zest.Pour into a shallow metal tray and freeze for 4 hours, scraping and stirring with a fork every 45 minutes so it stays smooth and fine.Blitz briefly in a food processor just before serving, scoop into cups and top with raspberries.DrinksInvisible ink lemon, ginger and mint fizzLemon, ginger syrup and muddled mint over crushed ice, topped with soda waterHow to make it150g caster sugar150ml water1 knob ginger (about 5cm), sliced1 cup mint leaves, plus sprigs200ml lemon juice800ml chilled soda water1 bag crushed iceSimmer the sugar, water and ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain.Muddle the mint with the lemon juice and ginger syrup in a jug.Fill four glasses with crushed ice, pour in the lemon mix and top with soda water.Garnish with lemon wheels and mint sprigs.Hot apple juice with cinnamonBrewed for a stake-out at the National Archives.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
